title_en: Yang Baoxi v. Tianjin Clothing Technical School — dispute over failure to perform statutory duties
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 42, paragraph 1, subparagraph (3) of the Education Law, students are entitled to obtain corresponding academic certificates after completing the prescribed studies. An educational institution's failure to directly issue graduation certificates to students it has approved for graduation constitutes a violation of law.
keywords_en: Administrative; Failure to perform statutory duties; First instance; Basic people's court; Tianjin; Natural person; Legal person; Education Law; Whether a school's failure to issue graduation certificates is illegal; Protection of the right to education; Plaintiff supported; Graduation certificate not issued; Academic credential; Enterprise-run school; Administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Yang Baoxi v. Tianjin Garment Technical School — case concerning failure to perform statutory duties

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 42, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Education Law, an educated person shall have the right to receive a corresponding academic certificate after completing the prescribed studies. An educational institution’s failure to directly issue a graduation certificate to an educated person whom it has approved for graduation constitutes an illegal act.

Plaintiff: Yang Baoxi, male, 29 years old, unemployed, residing at Heiniucheng Avenue, Hexi District, Tianjin.

Defendant: Tianjin Garment Technical School. Address: Ji'an Avenue, Hedong District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Wang Shiping, Principal of the school.

Third Party: Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd. Address: Chifeng Avenue, Heping District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Liu Baogen, Chairman of the company.

The plaintiff, Yang Baoxi, was a student of the class of 1991 at the defendant, Tianjin Garment Technical School (hereinafter referred to as Garment Technical School). When Yang Baoxi graduated in 1994, the defendant did not issue him a graduation certificate. On December 13, 2004, Yang Baoxi filed an administrative lawsuit with the Hedong District People's Court of Tianjin, on the ground that the Garment Technical School (formerly Tianjin Garment Technical Workers School) had failed to perform its statutory duties. Because Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Textile Group) has a legal interest in the act complained of in this case, the Hedong District People's Court, in accordance with law, notified Textile Group to participate in the proceedings as a third party.

The plaintiff alleged: In 1991, I applied for and was admitted to Garment Technical School. After graduating in 1994, Garment Technical School never issued me a graduation certificate. Although I urged them many times afterwards, the other party simply told the plaintiff to wait, resulting in my failure in numerous job applications over many years due to lack of academic credentials. In 2000, due to financial difficulties, I went astray. After being released from prison in 2004, I again requested Garment Technical School to issue the graduation certificate, and the other party issued a "Graduation Certificate" (xueli zhengming) on June 2 of that year. I request that the court order the defendant to fulfill its obligation to issue the graduation certificate.

Evidence provided by the plaintiff:

The Graduation Certificate issued by Garment Technical School on June 2, 2004, to prove that Garment Technical School did not issue him a graduation certificate.

The defendant argued: When the plaintiff graduated in 1994, our school issued him a graduation certificate in accordance with the student status management regulations. However, because our school is a school run by an enterprise, and graduates were uniformly assigned within the enterprise system, our school, as required, submitted all graduates' personnel files and graduation certificates to the Labor and Personnel Division of Tianjin Garment United Corporation. After the graduates were assigned, their employing enterprises would go to the corporation to collect the documents. The plaintiff did not report to the designated enterprise, Tianjin Garment No. 17 Factory, at the time of graduation. There were various reasons for his subsequent failure to find employment, which should not be attributed to the graduation certificate. At the beginning of 2004, he suddenly came to the school to request the graduation certificate and demand economic compensation. Our school clearly told him that the graduation certificate was not at the school and issued him an academic credential certificate. We request the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

Evidence provided by the defendant:

1. Jin Lao Pei Zi (1978) No. 240 Notice on Issuing the Arrangement of the Plan for Expanding Enrollment in Technical Schools in Tianjin in 1978 and the 1991 Enrollment Plan Table for Tianjin Technical Schools, issued by the Tianjin Municipal Labor Bureau, to prove that the defendant was lawfully established and the legality of enrollment in 1991.

2. The school's graduate assignment roster, to prove that the plaintiff was assigned to work at Tianjin Garment No. 17 Factory.

3. Testimony of the former principal of the defendant, Xiao Dehua, to prove that the personnel files and graduation certificates of the 1994 graduates were all submitted to the former Tianjin Garment Industry Company, and after students reported to their enterprises, the employing enterprises would go to the company to collect the files and graduation certificates.

The third party, Textile Group, argued: The defendant is an independent legal entity with the capacity to independently bear civil liability. The defendant was transferred to the affiliation of our company in February 2002, and now belongs to the knitwear company under our company. The issue of the graduation certificate, which occurred in 1994, has nothing to do with our company because at that time the school was not under our company's management. According to the provisions of Jin Zheng Han (2001) No. 72 of the Tianjin Municipal People's Government, our company currently does not assume functions of government administration, industry management, or social management. Our company has no responsibility for the school's issuance of certificates, and therefore has no interest in this case.

Evidence provided by the third party:

1. Jin Tiao Ban (1999) No. 63 Reply on the Transfer of the Whole Establishment of Tianjin Garment Technical School Affiliated to Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd. to the Management of Nankai District People's Government, issued by the Tianjin Municipal Adjustment Industry Office, to prove that the defendant was managed by the Nankai District Government.

2. Jin Zheng Han (2001) No. 72 Reply on Issues Concerning the Implementation Plan for Restructuring Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd., issued by the Tianjin Municipal People's Government, to prove the positioning of the third party's functions, i.e., it does not assume functions of government administration, industry management, or social management.

3. The document approved by the relevant leaders of the General Office of the Tianjin Municipal People's Government, Jin Jing Tiao (2002) No. 9 Request for Instructions on Issues Concerning the Adjustment of the Subordinate Relationship of Tianjin Garment Technical School, issued by the Tianjin Municipal Economic Commission, to prove the fact that in February 2002, Tianjin Garment Technical School, originally affiliated with Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd., was transferred back to the management of the third party.

4. Jin Jing Qi (2004) No. 4 Reply on Approving the Amendment of the Articles of Association of Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd., issued by the Tianjin Municipal Economic Commission, to prove that Tianjin Textile Industry Corporation and Tianjin Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd. were merged and restructured into Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd., and Tianjin Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd. became a wholly owned subsidiary of the third party, with the property rights of the original affiliated garment enterprises unchanged, and the original claims and debts still to be borne by that company.

The Hedong District People's Court of Tianjin confirmed the following facts in this case:

The defendant, Garment Technical School, was a technical school established with the approval of the former Tianjin Municipal Labor Bureau in 1978, and later changed to its current name. In 1991, the plaintiff, Yang Baoxi, applied for and was admitted to Garment Technical School. After completing all course studies with passing grades and graduating in 1994, Garment Technical School did not issue a graduation certificate to Yang Baoxi personally. In February 2002, Garment Technical School, originally affiliated with Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd., was transferred back to the management of the third party, Textile Group. On June 2, 2004, Yang Baoxi requested that Garment Technical School issue a replacement graduation certificate, but Garment Technical School only issued him an academic credential certificate and did not issue a replacement graduation certificate as requested by Yang Baoxi.

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the school's failure to directly issue a graduation certificate to a student it had approved for graduation constitutes an illegal act.

The Hedong District People's Court of Tianjin held:

According to Article 42, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Education Law of the People's Republic of China, an educated person shall have the right to receive a corresponding academic certificate after completing the prescribed studies.

The defendant, Garment Technical School, as a secondary vocational education school engaged in training skilled workers, should, in accordance with Article 42, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Education Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 30 of the Provisions on the Administration of Student Status in Technical Schools (Lao Bu Fa [1990] No. [ ]) issued by the Ministry of Labor on May 4, 1990, which states, "Students who have completed all courses specified in the teaching plan and have passed the graduation examination and overall evaluation (graduation assessment) shall be approved for graduation, and the school shall issue them graduation certificates," issue academic certificates to students who have received education at the school and completed the prescribed studies. The current Garment Technical School's act of not issuing a graduation certificate to Yang Baoxi on the ground that his graduation certificate had been submitted to the superior competent authority lacks a legal basis, infringes upon Yang Baoxi's right to education that he should enjoy according to law, and therefore the school shall bear corresponding legal liability. Although the third party, Textile Group, was not the competent authority of Garment Technical School at the time when the school failed to issue a graduation certificate to Yang Baoxi in 1994, after Garment Technical School, originally affiliated with Zhongfu International Group Co., Ltd., was transferred back to its management in February 2002, Textile Group, as the competent authority of the school, should assume the duty of supervision and management, promptly review the remaining issues of the school, and urge it to correct its illegal acts. Due to Textile Group's negligent management, the dispute in this case remained unresolved for a long period, ultimately leading to litigation. Therefore, Textile Group should bear a certain degree of responsibility. In light of the actual circumstances of this case, Textile Group should actively assist its subordinate Garment Technical School in handling the graduation certificate through the relevant labor administrative authorities, so as to effectively protect Yang Baoxi's legitimate rights and interests from infringement.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 54, paragraph (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 21 of the Education Law of the People's Republic of China, the Hedong District People's Court of Tianjin, on March 9, 2005, rendered the following judgment:

Within sixty days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, the defendant, Tianjin Garment Technical School, shall issue the graduation certificate to the plaintiff, Yang Baoxi, and the third party, Tianjin Textile Group (Holdings) Co., Ltd., shall assist in handling the matter.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by the defendant, Tianjin Garment Technical School.

After the judgment, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period. The judgment has taken legal effect.
